text:
5.19 CKD / ESKD composites & time variables
Ported from ICI-CKD §5.14. Variable names are kept identical to the source project — including eskd_defination_1 and the _after_ici suffix on the ESRD variables — so the two projects stay directly comparable. In this project the _after_ici suffix means “after baseline_sample_date”, i.e. after first platinum.


Code
final_master <- final_master %>%
  mutate(
    eskd_composite = ifelse(esrd_kt_after_ici == 1 | eskd_defination_1 == 1, 1L, 0L),
    eskd_composite = ifelse(is.na(eskd_composite), 0L, eskd_composite),
    eskd_composite_date = pmin(esrd_kt_after_ici_date, eskd_defination_1_date,
                               na.rm = TRUE),

    time_to_eskd_composite  = as.numeric(eskd_composite_date  - baseline_sample_date),
    time_to_ckd_incidence   = as.numeric(ckd_incidence_date   - baseline_sample_date),
    time_to_ckd_progression = as.numeric(ckd_progression_date - baseline_sample_date),

    time_to_ckd_incidence_any = as.numeric(ckd_incidence_any_date - baseline_sample_date),

    # CKD composite = CKD incidence + CKD progression + ESKD composite.
    # Uses ckd_incidence (the >25 % definition), not ckd_incidence_any.
    ckd_composite = ifelse(eskd_composite == 1 | ckd_incidence == 1 |
                           ckd_progression == 1, 1L, 0L),
    ckd_composite = ifelse(is.na(ckd_composite), 0L, ckd_composite),
    time_to_ckd_composite = pmin(time_to_eskd_composite,
                                 time_to_ckd_incidence,
                                 time_to_ckd_progression, na.rm = TRUE),

    last_cre_days  = as.numeric(last_cre_date - baseline_sample_date),
    aki_before_ckd = ifelse(!is.na(aki_days) & !is.na(time_to_ckd_composite) &
                            aki_days <= time_to_ckd_composite, 1L, 0L)
  )

# --- Long-horizon death, from the RPDR Dem file -------------------------------
# The existing death_90 / time_to_death_90 come from REDCap pt_status and are
# capped at 90 days, so they cannot serve as the competing event for outcomes
# that run to the end of creatinine follow-up. Two sources carry death at its
# actual time and they do not nest: RPDR Date_Of_Death gives a date, and REDCap
# pt_status == "Dead" means the last-follow-up date IS the death date. Some
# deaths appear in only one of the two, so death_days_any below takes the union.
final_master <- final_master %>%
  left_join(dem, by = "EMPI") %>%
  mutate(
    rpdr_deceased  = ifelse(is.na(rpdr_deceased), 0L, rpdr_deceased),
    death_days_lt  = as.numeric(death_date - baseline_sample_date),
    # A death recorded before baseline is a data error; treat as unknown.
    death_days_lt  = ifelse(!is.na(death_days_lt) & death_days_lt < 0,
                            NA_real_, death_days_lt),
    death_lt       = ifelse(!is.na(death_days_lt), 1L, 0L)
  )

cat("RPDR deceased:", sum(final_master$rpdr_deceased == 1),
    " with a usable death date:", sum(final_master$death_lt == 1),
    " (deceased but undated, censored instead:",
    sum(final_master$rpdr_deceased == 1 & final_master$death_lt == 0), ")\n")

section: 6.1 Note: Record 911 — All RPDR Pre-Baseline Labs Missing
text:
6.1 Note: Record 911 — All RPDR Pre-Baseline Labs Missing
Record 911 (baseline_sample_date = 2025-08-19) has valid REDCap baseline labs (baseline_cre = 0.93, baseline_cys_c = 0.88, cockcroft = 83.4) but all RPDR pre-baseline labs are NA (pre_HGB_45days, pre_PLT_45days, pre_ALB_45days, pre_CRE_45days).
Root cause: This patient has 73 RPDR lab records, but the closest labs before baseline were drawn on 2025-02-11 — 189 days before baseline, well outside the 45-day pre_lab() window. No RPDR labs exist between 2025-07-05 and 2025-08-19.
Impact: This patient is dropped from Fine-Gray models via complete-case analysis whenever pre_HGB_45days, pre_PLT_45days, or pre_CRE_45days appears as a covariate (i.e., all models except base-only AKI models). Their cockcroft, ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex, and egfr_ratio are valid.

title: Ritu Project — Summary
text:
Competing-Risk Models (death competing)
Fine-Gray models for egfr_diff_pct_per10 are in §4.12–4.13 of the whole and entire pages and §5.12–5.13 of the carboplatin pages. These are the only two long-horizon outcomes modelled; the 90-day adverse-event and hospitalization outcomes are modelled with the 90-day competing event in §4 / §5.
The competing event is death at any time, death_days_any — death_90 is capped at 90 days and cannot place a death in time beyond day 90, so it cannot serve over a multi-year horizon. death_days_any is the union of the two sources that carry a death date: the RPDR Date_Of_Death when there is one, otherwise the REDCap last-follow-up date for a patient whose pt_status is “Dead”. The two do not nest — 22 REDCap deaths have no RPDR date, and RPDR dates deaths REDCap has not caught up with — so the union gives 300 dated deaths in the entire cohort against 278 from RPDR alone, and 37 against 34 in Local/Early. Someone flagged deceased in RPDR with no date who is still alive in REDCap stays censored. Censoring is at the last creatinine.

title: Ritu Project — Entire Cohort (All Stages)
text:
Entire cohort — all tumour stages. This page runs the same analysis as the Local/Early page on the unrestricted cohort: N = 943 (322 Local/Early + 621 Advanced/Metastatic; 596 carboplatin, 347 cisplatin). It reads ritu_full_master.rds, saved by ritu_data.qmd immediately before the stage restriction, so every variable is identical — including the creatinine from the Ritu_project RPDR pull and the CKD / ESKD / AKI family.
tumor_stage is a covariate again here. It is constant in the Local/Early cohort and therefore dropped there; in the entire cohort it varies, so it is restored to Table 1 and to every Fine-Gray, cause-specific, Cox and linear-subHR adjuster set. That makes this page’s model specification the same as the Jiaxuan project’s.
Only the long-horizon kidney outcomes are modelled on this page. AKI within 1 year and the CKD composite are carried through Fine-Gray competing-risk models in Section 4, with death at any time as the competing event. The 90-day adverse-event, hospitalization and 90-day-death models this page used to carry have been removed; those outcomes are still derived in Data Management and remain in the saved master, they are simply no longer modelled. Read both models with their event counts in view — 197 AKI and 70 CKD-composite events in 943 patients against ~20 covariate degrees of freedom, so both are over-parameterised. See RITU_PROJECT.md.

title: Ritu Project — Entire Cohort (All Stages)
section: 2.1 Follow-up time (days from baseline to last known status)
text:
2.1 Follow-up time (days from baseline to last known status)
days_last_follow_up = last_follow_up_date − baseline_sample_date. Two alternative definitions of “follow-up time” are shown side-by-side so the reader can pick the most defensible one for their purpose:

A — Raw days: unrestricted calendar follow-up (median dominated by patients who kept returning for years).
B — Raw days, ≤ 365 days: restricts to patients whose last-known contact was within 1 year of baseline (drops the long tail of years-later return visits; more comparable across patients).



Code
followup_summary <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(record_id, platin_group, days_last_follow_up) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(days_last_follow_up)

fmt_med_iqr <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0) return("—")
  sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", median(x), quantile(x, 0.25), quantile(x, 0.75))
}

groups_split <- function(f) {
  x_all <- f(followup_summary$days_last_follow_up)
  x_cis <- f(followup_summary$days_last_follow_up[followup_summary$platin_group == "Cisplatin"])
  x_car <- f(followup_summary$days_last_follow_up[followup_summary$platin_group == "Carboplatin"])
  list(Overall = x_all, Cisplatin = x_cis, Carboplatin = x_car)
}

fu_row <- function(label, xs) {
  tibble::tibble(
    Interpretation                      = label,
    `Overall N`                         = length(xs$Overall),
    `Overall — Median [IQR] (days)`     = fmt_med_iqr(xs$Overall),
    `Cisplatin N`                       = length(xs$Cisplatin),
    `Cisplatin — Median [IQR] (days)`   = fmt_med_iqr(xs$Cisplatin),
    `Carboplatin N`                     = length(xs$Carboplatin),
    `Carboplatin — Median [IQR] (days)` = fmt_med_iqr(xs$Carboplatin)
  )
}

def_A <- function(v) v
def_B <- function(v) v[v <= 365]

followup_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fu_row("A — Raw days",             groups_split(def_A)),
  fu_row("B — Raw days, ≤ 365 days", groups_split(def_B))
)

flextable::flextable(followup_tbl) |>
  flextable::set_caption("Follow-up time from baseline to last known status (whole cohort). Two alternative definitions shown side-by-side.") |>
  flextable::autofit()

title: Ritu Project — Entire Cohort (All Stages)
text:
2.2 Long-Horizon Kidney Outcomes (CKD / ESKD / AKI)
Ported from the ICI-CKD project and built in Sections 5.16–5.19 of Data Management. Creatinine for these comes from the Ritu_project RPDR pull (Oct 2026).

None of these are censored at 90 days. A qualifying CKD episode has to be sustained for ≥ 90 days, so they run over the full length of RPDR creatinine follow-up. aki is restricted to events within 1 year. This section reports all of them descriptively; aki and ckd_composite are the two that are modelled — see the Fine-Gray section below. The rest are descriptive only.

Definitions as of the latest revision. aki is now restricted to events within 1 year of baseline (aki_any keeps the unrestricted count for reference and is not modelled). ckd_incidence uses a > 25 % eGFR drop; ckd_incidence_any drops the percent requirement entirely; ckd_progression now additionally requires a > 30 % further drop, where it previously counted any patient who was simply below 60 before and after — which flagged stable CKD as progression and is why that count fell sharply.
aki is also not the same variable as AKI_g2_90days / AKI_kdigo_90days: it compares each creatinine against the patient’s own preceding 90-day median (or 2-day low) rather than against a fixed pre-baseline value. The cross-tabulation below shows how far the two diverge.
📄 Download Word table


Code
.kid_row <- function(flag, time_var, label) {
  n <- sum(dat[[flag]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  tt <- if (!is.null(time_var) && time_var %in% names(dat))
          dat[[time_var]][dat[[flag]] == 1] else NA_real_
  tibble::tibble(
    Outcome = label,
    `n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / nrow(dat)),
    `Median days to event (IQR)` = if (n > 0 && any(!is.na(tt)))
        sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", median(tt, na.rm = TRUE),
                quantile(tt, .25, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(tt, .75, na.rm = TRUE))
      else "-"
  )
}

  .kid_row("eskd_defination_1", NULL,                          "ESKD (eGFR <10, sustained >=90d)"),

NoteWhy anchor at the median (subHR = 1 at the reference)



Three reasons to anchor at the median:

Interpretability: “A patient with eGFR ratio of 0.8 has ~1.5× the subHR compared to a typical patient (at the median).”
Stability: The median sits in the densest part of the data, so estimates near it have the tightest confidence intervals. The CIs fan out as you move away — you can see this in the plots.
No arbitrary choice: If we picked 1.0 arbitrarily, the plot would look almost identical here (because median ≈ 1), but in cohorts where the median is 0.9 or 1.1, picking 1.0 would either shift or distort the curve without changing the actual model.

section: 7.0 Summary table: Fine-Gray subHR per 10 mL/min decline in eGFR discrepancy
text:
7.0 Summary table: Fine-Gray subHR per 10 mL/min decline in eGFR discrepancy
One row per outcome. Multivariable Fine-Gray model fit with egfr_disc_per10dec = -egfr_discrepancy / 10 (positive when CKD-EPI Cr-Cys is below CG) plus the same adjusters used by the curves below. The HR for egfr_disc_per10dec is the multiplicative change in subHR per 10 mL/min lower eGFR discrepancy. 90-day death uses Cox PH (no competing event); all other outcomes use Fine-Gray with death as the competing event. p-values in this summary table are raw Wald (not Bonferroni-adjusted); the plot subtitles in Sections 7.1–7.11 apply Bonferroni correction across the six primary AE outcomes.
📄 Download Word table


Code
.disc_adj_set <- function(pre_labs = NULL) {
  base_adj <- c("age","sex","score","ecog_score_cat2",
                "cancer_type_cat_7","tumor_stage","platin_group","high_dose",
                "Paclitaxel","Pemetrexed","Gemcitabine","ici",
                "bmi","smoking","steroids","thyroid")
  if (!is.null(pre_labs)) base_adj <- c(base_adj, pre_labs)
  base_adj
}

fg_disc_row <- function(time_var, status_var, label, pre_labs = NULL) {
  adj <- .disc_adj_set(pre_labs)
  d <- dat %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(c("egfr_disc_per10dec", time_var, status_var, adj))) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na()
  adj_df <- d[, adj, drop = FALSE]
  X_adj  <- model.matrix(~ ., data = adj_df)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  X      <- cbind(egfr_disc_per10dec = d$egfr_disc_per10dec, X_adj)
  stat_num <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(as.character(d[[status_var]])))
  time_num <- as.numeric(d[[time_var]])
  fit <- cmprsk::crr(time_num, stat_num, cov1 = X, failcode = 1)
  b <- unname(fit$coef[1]); se <- sqrt(fit$var[1, 1])
  hr <- exp(b); lcl <- exp(b - 1.96 * se); ucl <- exp(b + 1.96 * se)
  pv <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(b / se)))
  tibble(
    Outcome = label,
    Model   = "Fine-Gray",
    N       = nrow(d),
    `Excluded (missing cov.)` = nrow(dat) - nrow(d),
    Events  = sum(stat_num == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    `(sub)HR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", hr, lcl, ucl),
    `p-value` = ifelse(pv < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", pv))
  )
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
fg_disc_row <- .wrap_row(fg_disc_row)


cox_disc_row <- function(time_var, status_var, label, pre_labs = NULL) {
  adj <- .disc_adj_set(pre_labs)
  d <- dat %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(c("egfr_disc_per10dec", time_var, status_var, adj))) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na()
  fmla <- as.formula(paste0("Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var,
                            ") ~ egfr_disc_per10dec + ",
                            paste(adj, collapse = " + ")))
  fit <- survival::coxph(fmla, data = d)
  b   <- unname(coef(fit)["egfr_disc_per10dec"])
  se  <- sqrt(vcov(fit)["egfr_disc_per10dec", "egfr_disc_per10dec"])
  hr  <- exp(b); lcl <- exp(b - 1.96 * se); ucl <- exp(b + 1.96 * se)
  pv  <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(b / se)))
  tibble(
    Outcome = label,
    Model   = "Cox PH",
    N       = nrow(d),
    `Excluded (missing cov.)` = nrow(dat) - nrow(d),
    Events  = sum(d[[status_var]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    `(sub)HR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", hr, lcl, ucl),
    `p-value` = ifelse(pv < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", pv))
  )
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
cox_disc_row <- .wrap_row(cox_disc_row)

plot_subhr_linear_disc <- function(time_var, status_var, extra_adj = NULL,
                                   outcome_label, n_bonf = 6) {
  base_adj <- c("age","sex","score","ecog_score_cat2",
                "cancer_type_cat_7","tumor_stage","platin_group","high_dose",
                "Paclitaxel","Pemetrexed","Gemcitabine","ici",
                "bmi","smoking","steroids","thyroid")
  keep <- c("egfr_discrepancy", time_var, status_var, base_adj, extra_adj)
  d <- dat %>% dplyr::select(all_of(keep)) %>% tidyr::drop_na()

  adj_df <- d[, c(base_adj, extra_adj), drop = FALSE]
  X_adj <- model.matrix(~ ., data = adj_df)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  X <- cbind(egfr_discrepancy = d$egfr_discrepancy, X_adj)

  stat_num <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(as.character(d[[status_var]])))
  time_num <- as.numeric(d[[time_var]])

  fit <- cmprsk::crr(ftime = time_num, fstatus = stat_num,
                     cov1 = X, failcode = 1)

  beta   <- fit$coef[1]
  V_beta <- fit$var[1, 1]
  se_b   <- sqrt(V_beta)

  # subHR summaries: per 1 mL/min, and per IQR (Q3 - Q1) of egfr_discrepancy
  q1    <- as.numeric(quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE))
  q3    <- as.numeric(quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE))
  iqr_w <- q3 - q1
  # per 10 mL/min DECLINE: HR = exp(-10 * beta); SE on log scale = 10 * se_b
  hr10  <- exp(-10 * beta);       hr10_l <- exp(-10 * beta - 1.96 * 10 * se_b);     hr10_u <- exp(-10 * beta + 1.96 * 10 * se_b)
  # per IQR DECLINE: HR = exp(-iqr_w * beta); SE on log scale = |iqr_w| * se_b
  hri   <- exp(-iqr_w * beta);    hri_l <- exp(-iqr_w * beta - 1.96 * abs(iqr_w) * se_b); hri_u <- exp(-iqr_w * beta + 1.96 * abs(iqr_w) * se_b)
  pval  <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(beta / se_b)))
  pval_bonf <- min(pval * n_bonf, 1)
  p_shown <- if (n_bonf > 1) pval_bonf else pval
  p_lbl   <- if (n_bonf > 1) sprintf("p_Bonf = %s (n = %d)", ifelse(p_shown < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p_shown)), n_bonf) else sprintf("p = %s", ifelse(p_shown < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p_shown)))
  subtitle_str <- sprintf(
    "subHR per 10 mL/min decline: %.2f (%.2f-%.2f), %s  |  per IQR decline (Δ = %.1f): %.2f (%.2f-%.2f)  |  IQR: [%.1f, %.1f]",
    hr10, hr10_l, hr10_u, p_lbl, iqr_w, hri, hri_l, hri_u, q1, q3)

  ref_x  <- median(d$egfr_discrepancy, na.rm = TRUE)
  grid_x <- seq(quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
                quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
                length.out = 100)

  log_hr <- beta * (grid_x - ref_x)
  se     <- sqrt((grid_x - ref_x)^2 * V_beta)

  df_plot <- tibble(
    x     = grid_x,
    subhr = exp(log_hr),
    lcl   = exp(log_hr - 1.96 * se),
    ucl   = exp(log_hr + 1.96 * se)
  )

  ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = x, y = subhr)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), alpha = 0.2, fill = "darkorange") +
    geom_line(color = "darkorange", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ref_x, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey40") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(q1, q3), linetype = "dashed",
               color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(x = "eGFR Discrepancy (mL/min)",
         y = "subHR (95% CI)",

plot_cox_linear_disc <- function(time_var, status_var, extra_adj = NULL,
                                 outcome_label, n_bonf = 6) {
  base_adj <- c("age","sex","score","ecog_score_cat2",
                "cancer_type_cat_7","tumor_stage","platin_group","high_dose",
                "Paclitaxel","Pemetrexed","Gemcitabine","ici",
                "bmi","smoking","steroids","thyroid")
  keep <- c("egfr_discrepancy", time_var, status_var, base_adj, extra_adj)
  d <- dat %>% dplyr::select(all_of(keep)) %>% tidyr::drop_na()

  fmla <- as.formula(paste0(
    "Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ egfr_discrepancy + ",
    paste(c(base_adj, extra_adj), collapse = " + ")
  ))
  fit <- survival::coxph(fmla, data = d)

  beta   <- coef(fit)["egfr_discrepancy"]
  V_beta <- vcov(fit)["egfr_discrepancy", "egfr_discrepancy"]
  se_b   <- sqrt(V_beta)

  q1    <- as.numeric(quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE))
  q3    <- as.numeric(quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE))
  iqr_w <- q3 - q1
  hr10  <- exp(-10 * beta);       hr10_l <- exp(-10 * beta - 1.96 * 10 * se_b);     hr10_u <- exp(-10 * beta + 1.96 * 10 * se_b)
  hri   <- exp(-iqr_w * beta);    hri_l <- exp(-iqr_w * beta - 1.96 * abs(iqr_w) * se_b); hri_u <- exp(-iqr_w * beta + 1.96 * abs(iqr_w) * se_b)
  pval  <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(beta / se_b)))
  pval_bonf <- min(pval * n_bonf, 1)
  p_shown <- if (n_bonf > 1) pval_bonf else pval
  p_lbl   <- if (n_bonf > 1) sprintf("p_Bonf = %s (n = %d)", ifelse(p_shown < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p_shown)), n_bonf) else sprintf("p = %s", ifelse(p_shown < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p_shown)))
  subtitle_str <- sprintf(
    "HR per 10 mL/min decline: %.2f (%.2f-%.2f), %s  |  per IQR decline (Δ = %.1f): %.2f (%.2f-%.2f)  |  IQR: [%.1f, %.1f]",
    hr10, hr10_l, hr10_u, p_lbl, iqr_w, hri, hri_l, hri_u, q1, q3)

  ref_x  <- median(d$egfr_discrepancy, na.rm = TRUE)
  grid_x <- seq(quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
                quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
                length.out = 100)

  log_hr <- beta * (grid_x - ref_x)
  se     <- sqrt((grid_x - ref_x)^2 * V_beta)

  df_plot <- tibble(
    x   = grid_x,
    hr  = exp(log_hr),
    lcl = exp(log_hr - 1.96 * se),
    ucl = exp(log_hr + 1.96 * se)
  )

  ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = x, y = hr)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), alpha = 0.2, fill = "darkorange") +
    geom_line(color = "darkorange", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ref_x, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey40") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(q1, q3), linetype = "dashed",
               color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(x = "eGFR Discrepancy (mL/min)",
         y = "HR (95% CI)",
         title = outcome_label,
         subtitle = subtitle_str) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 4)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey25"))
}

9.7 – 8.12 eGFR Difference (%) distribution by category
For each of the same six splits as 10.1 – 10.6, overlaid kernel density curves of the eGFR difference (%) = 100 × (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed − Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault. Red = highlighted level (≥ threshold, or Female for the sex panel); grey = reference level. Dashed grey vertical line marks the 0 % concordance point; dotted verticals mark each group’s median. Subtitle carries N and median for each level plus a two-sided Mann-Whitney U p-value (equivalent to Wilcoxon rank-sum) comparing the two distributions.


Code
plot_ratio_by_group <- function(highlight_var, threshold, label,
                                highlight_label, reference_label) {
  d <- dat %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(egfr_diff_pct), !is.na(.data[[highlight_var]])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(grp = factor(
      ifelse(.data[[highlight_var]] >= threshold, highlight_label, reference_label),
      levels = c(highlight_label, reference_label)))

  med_tbl <- d %>%
    dplyr::group_by(grp) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(m = median(egfr_diff_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
                     n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

  pval <- tryCatch(
    wilcox.test(egfr_diff_pct ~ grp, data = d)$p.value,
    error = function(e) NA_real_)
  p_str <- if (is.na(pval)) "NA" else
    ifelse(pval < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", pval))

  col_vec <- setNames(c("#E31A1C", "grey50"),
                      c(highlight_label, reference_label))

  ggplot(d, aes(x = egfr_diff_pct, fill = grp, color = grp)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
    geom_vline(data = med_tbl, aes(xintercept = m, color = grp),
               linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = col_vec) +
    scale_color_manual(values = col_vec) +
    labs(x = "eGFR difference (%): 100 × (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys − CG) / CG",
         y = "Density",
         fill = NULL, color = NULL,
         title = label,
         subtitle = sprintf(
           "%s: N = %d, median = %.1f %%   |   %s: N = %d, median = %.1f %%   |   Mann-Whitney U p = %s",
           highlight_label,
           med_tbl$n[med_tbl$grp == highlight_label],
           med_tbl$m[med_tbl$grp == highlight_label],
           reference_label,
           med_tbl$n[med_tbl$grp == reference_label],
           med_tbl$m[med_tbl$grp == reference_label],
           p_str)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey25"))
}

title: Ritu Project — Carboplatin Cohort (Local/Early)
text:
Ritu cohort — Local/Early stage only. This page repeats the Jiaxuan carboplatin analysis on the subset of patients with tumor_stage == "Local/Early", leaving N = 189 carboplatin patients. tumor_stage is dropped from Table 1 and from every adjuster set because it is constant within this cohort. Everything else is unchanged.
Only the long-horizon kidney outcomes are modelled on this page. AKI within 1 year and the CKD composite are carried through Fine-Gray competing-risk models in Section 5, with death at any time as the competing event. The 90-day adverse-event, hospitalization and 90-day-death models this page used to carry have been removed; those outcomes are still derived in Data Management and remain in the saved master, they are simply no longer modelled. Read both models with their event counts in view — 23 AKI and 11 CKD-composite events in 189 patients against ~20 covariate degrees of freedom, so both are over-parameterised. See RITU_PROJECT.md.

2.2 Signed Dose Discrepancy Distribution
Smooth kernel density estimate of the signed dose discrepancy (actual − predicted, CKD-EPI Cr-Cys). The area under the curve is shaded by sign — negative (under-dosed region) on one side, positive on the other.


Code
dose_vals <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(dose_discrepancy)) %>%
  pull(dose_discrepancy)

dens <- density(dose_vals, n = 512)
y_at_zero <- approx(dens$x, dens$y, xout = 0)$y

dens_df <- tibble(x = dens$x, y = dens$y) %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(x = 0, y = y_at_zero)) %>%
  arrange(x)

neg_part <- dens_df %>% filter(x <= 0) %>% mutate(side = "neg")
pos_part <- dens_df %>% filter(x >= 0) %>% mutate(side = "pos")
plot_df  <- bind_rows(neg_part, pos_part)

ggplot() +
  geom_area(data = plot_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = side), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = dens_df, aes(x = x, y = y), linewidth = 0.6, color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 25, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(neg = "#E31A1C", pos = "grey60"),
                    guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-250, 250), ylim = c(0, 0.010)) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Signed Dose Discrepancy (Carboplatin)",
       x = "Dose Discrepancy (mg) = Actual dose – Predicted dose",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

title: Ritu Project — Carboplatin Cohort (Local/Early)
text:
3.2 Long-Horizon Kidney Outcomes (CKD / ESKD / AKI)
Ported from the ICI-CKD project and built in Sections 5.16–5.19 of Data Management. Creatinine for these comes from the Ritu_project RPDR pull (Oct 2026).

None of these are censored at 90 days. A qualifying CKD episode has to be sustained for ≥ 90 days, so they run over the full length of RPDR creatinine follow-up. aki is restricted to events within 1 year. This section reports all of them descriptively; aki and ckd_composite are the two that are modelled — see the Fine-Gray section below. The rest are descriptive only.

Definitions as of the latest revision. aki is now restricted to events within 1 year of baseline (aki_any keeps the unrestricted count for reference and is not modelled). ckd_incidence uses a > 25 % eGFR drop; ckd_incidence_any drops the percent requirement entirely; ckd_progression now additionally requires a > 30 % further drop, where it previously counted any patient who was simply below 60 before and after — which flagged stable CKD as progression and is why that count fell sharply.
aki is also not the same variable as AKI_g2_90days / AKI_kdigo_90days: it compares each creatinine against the patient’s own preceding 90-day median (or 2-day low) rather than against a fixed pre-baseline value. The cross-tabulation below shows how far the two diverge.
📄 Download Word table


Code
.kid_row <- function(flag, time_var, label) {
  n <- sum(dat[[flag]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  tt <- if (!is.null(time_var) && time_var %in% names(dat))
          dat[[time_var]][dat[[flag]] == 1] else NA_real_
  tibble::tibble(
    Outcome = label,
    `n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / nrow(dat)),
    `Median days to event (IQR)` = if (n > 0 && any(!is.na(tt)))
        sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", median(tt, na.rm = TRUE),
                quantile(tt, .25, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(tt, .75, na.rm = TRUE))
      else "-"
  )
}

kidney_lt <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  .kid_row("aki",               "aki_days",                    "AKI within 1 year (serial creatinine)"),
  .kid_row("aki_any",           "aki_days_any",                "AKI at any time (reference only, not modelled)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_incidence",     "time_to_ckd_incidence",       "CKD incidence (>25% eGFR drop to <60, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_incidence_any", "time_to_ckd_incidence_any",   "CKD incidence any (>=60 to <60, sustained >=90d, no % drop)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_progression",   "time_to_ckd_progression",     "CKD progression (<60 at baseline, further >30% drop, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("eskd_defination_1", NULL,                          "ESKD (eGFR <10, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("esrd_kt_after_ici", NULL,                          "ESRD / kidney transplant after baseline"),
  .kid_row("eskd_composite",    "time_to_eskd_composite",      "ESKD composite"),
  .kid_row("ckd_composite",     "time_to_ckd_composite",       "CKD composite (incidence + progression + ESKD composite)")
)

ft_kid <- flextable::flextable(kidney_lt) |>
  flextable::set_caption(sprintf(
    "Long-horizon kidney outcomes (N = %d). Not censored at 90 days.", nrow(dat))) |>
  flextable::autofit()
flextable::save_as_docx(ft_kid, path = file.path(docx_dir, "sec3_kidney_longhorizon.docx"))

NoteWhy anchor at the median (subHR = 1 at the reference)



Three reasons to anchor at the median:

Interpretability: “A patient with eGFR ratio of 0.8 has ~1.5× the subHR compared to a typical patient (at the median).”
Stability: The median sits in the densest part of the data, so estimates near it have the tightest confidence intervals. The CIs fan out as you move away — you can see this in the plots.
No arbitrary choice: If we picked 1.0 arbitrarily, the plot would look almost identical here (because median ≈ 1), but in cohorts where the median is 0.9 or 1.1, picking 1.0 would either shift or distort the curve without changing the actual model.

section: 10.0 Summary table: Fine-Gray subHR per 10 mL/min decline in eGFR discrepancy
text:
10.0 Summary table: Fine-Gray subHR per 10 mL/min decline in eGFR discrepancy
One row per outcome. Multivariable Fine-Gray model fit with egfr_disc_per10dec = -egfr_discrepancy / 10 (positive when CKD-EPI Cr-Cys is below CG) plus the same adjusters used by the curves below (no platin_group in the carboplatin-only cohort). The HR for egfr_disc_per10dec is the multiplicative change in subHR per 10 mL/min lower eGFR discrepancy. 90-day death uses Cox PH. p-values in this summary table are raw Wald (not Bonferroni-adjusted); the plot subtitles in Sections 10.1–10.11 apply Bonferroni correction across the six primary AE outcomes.
📄 Download Word table

.disc_adj_set <- function(pre_labs = NULL) {
  base_adj <- c("age","sex","score","ecog_score_cat2",
                "cancer_type_cat_7","high_dose",
                "Paclitaxel","Pemetrexed","Gemcitabine","ici",
                "bmi","smoking","steroids","thyroid")
  if (!is.null(pre_labs)) base_adj <- c(base_adj, pre_labs)
  base_adj
}

fg_disc_row <- function(time_var, status_var, label, pre_labs = NULL) {
  adj <- .disc_adj_set(pre_labs)
  d <- dat %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(c("egfr_disc_per10dec", time_var, status_var, adj))) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na()
  adj_df <- d[, adj, drop = FALSE]
  X_adj  <- model.matrix(~ ., data = adj_df)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  X      <- cbind(egfr_disc_per10dec = d$egfr_disc_per10dec, X_adj)
  stat_num <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(as.character(d[[status_var]])))
  time_num <- as.numeric(d[[time_var]])
  fit <- cmprsk::crr(time_num, stat_num, cov1 = X, failcode = 1)
  b <- unname(fit$coef[1]); se <- sqrt(fit$var[1, 1])
  hr <- exp(b); lcl <- exp(b - 1.96 * se); ucl <- exp(b + 1.96 * se)
  pv <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(b / se)))
  tibble(
    Outcome = label,
    Model   = "Fine-Gray",
    N       = nrow(d),
    `Excluded (missing cov.)` = nrow(dat) - nrow(d),
    Events  = sum(stat_num == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    `(sub)HR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", hr, lcl, ucl),
    `p-value` = ifelse(pv < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", pv))
  )
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
fg_disc_row <- .wrap_row(fg_disc_row)


cox_disc_row <- function(time_var, status_var, label, pre_labs = NULL) {
  adj <- .disc_adj_set(pre_labs)
  d <- dat %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(c("egfr_disc_per10dec", time_var, status_var, adj))) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na()
  fmla <- as.formula(paste0("Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var,
                            ") ~ egfr_disc_per10dec + ",
                            paste(adj, collapse = " + ")))
  fit <- survival::coxph(fmla, data = d)
  b   <- unname(coef(fit)["egfr_disc_per10dec"])
  se  <- sqrt(vcov(fit)["egfr_disc_per10dec", "egfr_disc_per10dec"])
  hr  <- exp(b); lcl <- exp(b - 1.96 * se); ucl <- exp(b + 1.96 * se)
  pv  <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(b / se)))
  tibble(
    Outcome = label,
    Model   = "Cox PH",
    N       = nrow(d),
    `Excluded (missing cov.)` = nrow(dat) - nrow(d),
    Events  = sum(d[[status_var]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    `(sub)HR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", hr, lcl, ucl),
    `p-value` = ifelse(pv < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", pv))
  )
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
cox_disc_row <- .wrap_row(cox_disc_row)

                "bmi","smoking","steroids","thyroid")
  keep <- c("egfr_discrepancy", time_var, status_var, base_adj, extra_adj)
  d <- dat %>% dplyr::select(all_of(keep)) %>% tidyr::drop_na()

  adj_df <- d[, c(base_adj, extra_adj), drop = FALSE]
  X_adj <- model.matrix(~ ., data = adj_df)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  X <- cbind(egfr_discrepancy = d$egfr_discrepancy, X_adj)

  stat_num <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(as.character(d[[status_var]])))
  time_num <- as.numeric(d[[time_var]])

  fit <- cmprsk::crr(ftime = time_num, fstatus = stat_num,
                     cov1 = X, failcode = 1)

  beta   <- fit$coef[1]
  V_beta <- fit$var[1, 1]
  se_b   <- sqrt(V_beta)

  q1    <- as.numeric(quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE))
  q3    <- as.numeric(quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE))
  iqr_w <- q3 - q1
  hr10  <- exp(-10 * beta);       hr10_l <- exp(-10 * beta - 1.96 * 10 * se_b);     hr10_u <- exp(-10 * beta + 1.96 * 10 * se_b)
  hri   <- exp(-iqr_w * beta);    hri_l <- exp(-iqr_w * beta - 1.96 * abs(iqr_w) * se_b); hri_u <- exp(-iqr_w * beta + 1.96 * abs(iqr_w) * se_b)
  pval  <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(beta / se_b)))
  pval_bonf <- min(pval * n_bonf, 1)
  p_shown <- if (n_bonf > 1) pval_bonf else pval
  p_lbl   <- if (n_bonf > 1) sprintf("p_Bonf = %s (n = %d)", ifelse(p_shown < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p_shown)), n_bonf) else sprintf("p = %s", ifelse(p_shown < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p_shown)))
  subtitle_str <- sprintf(
    "subHR per 10 mL/min decline: %.2f (%.2f-%.2f), %s  |  per IQR decline (Δ = %.1f): %.2f (%.2f-%.2f)  |  IQR: [%.1f, %.1f]",
    hr10, hr10_l, hr10_u, p_lbl, iqr_w, hri, hri_l, hri_u, q1, q3)

  ref_x  <- median(d$egfr_discrepancy, na.rm = TRUE)
  grid_x <- seq(quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
                quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
                length.out = 100)

  log_hr <- beta * (grid_x - ref_x)
  se     <- sqrt((grid_x - ref_x)^2 * V_beta)

  df_plot <- tibble(
    x     = grid_x,
    subhr = exp(log_hr),
    lcl   = exp(log_hr - 1.96 * se),
    ucl   = exp(log_hr + 1.96 * se)
  )

  ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = x, y = subhr)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), alpha = 0.2, fill = "darkorange") +
    geom_line(color = "darkorange", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ref_x, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey40") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(q1, q3), linetype = "dashed",
               color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(x = "eGFR Discrepancy (mL/min)",
         y = "subHR (95% CI)",
         title = outcome_label,
         subtitle = subtitle_str) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 4)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey25"))
}

plot_cox_linear_egfrdisc <- function(time_var, status_var, extra_adj = NULL,
                                     outcome_label, n_bonf = 6) {

    "Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ egfr_discrepancy + ",
    paste(c(base_adj, extra_adj), collapse = " + ")
  ))
  fit <- survival::coxph(fmla, data = d)

  beta   <- coef(fit)["egfr_discrepancy"]
  V_beta <- vcov(fit)["egfr_discrepancy", "egfr_discrepancy"]

  hri   <- exp(-iqr_w * beta);    hri_l <- exp(-iqr_w * beta - 1.96 * abs(iqr_w) * se_b); hri_u <- exp(-iqr_w * beta + 1.96 * abs(iqr_w) * se_b)
  pval  <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(beta / se_b)))
  pval_bonf <- min(pval * n_bonf, 1)

  p_lbl   <- if (n_bonf > 1) sprintf("p_Bonf = %s (n = %d)", ifelse(p_shown < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p_shown)), n_bonf) else sprintf("p = %s", ifelse(p_shown < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p_shown)))
  subtitle_str <- sprintf(
    "HR per 10 mL/min decline: %.2f (%.2f-%.2f), %s  |  per IQR decline (Δ = %.1f): %.2f (%.2f-%.2f)  |  IQR: [%.1f, %.1f]",
    hr10, hr10_l, hr10_u, p_lbl, iqr_w, hri, hri_l, hri_u, q1, q3)

  ref_x  <- median(d$egfr_discrepancy, na.rm = TRUE)
  grid_x <- seq(quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
                quantile(d$egfr_discrepancy, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
                length.out = 100)

  log_hr <- beta * (grid_x - ref_x)

  df_plot <- tibble(
    x   = grid_x,
    hr  = exp(log_hr),
    lcl = exp(log_hr - 1.96 * se),
    ucl = exp(log_hr + 1.96 * se)
  )

  ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = x, y = hr)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), alpha = 0.2, fill = "darkorange") +
    geom_line(color = "darkorange", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ref_x, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey40") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(q1, q3), linetype = "dashed",
               color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(x = "eGFR Discrepancy (mL/min)",
         y = "HR (95% CI)",
         title = outcome_label,
         subtitle = subtitle_str) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 4)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +

title: Ritu Project — Data Management
section: 5.16b Delta eGFR (creatinine) vs baseline at 90 / 180 / 365 days
text:
5.16b Delta eGFR (creatinine) vs baseline at 90 / 180 / 365 days
Change in creatinine-based eGFR from baseline at three fixed post-baseline marks. For each mark the creatinine closest to that day is used, provided it falls within DGFR_WINDOW days of it.
DGFR_WINDOW is 45 days: it matches the window this pipeline already uses for baseline labs (pre_CRE_45days), and it is the widest window that keeps the 90-day and 180-day marks from drawing on the same measurement (at +/- 90 days their intervals would be 0-180 and 90-270). Taken without a window the closest creatinine to day 365 is more than 276 days away for a tenth of the cohort, so an unwindowed value would not be a 365-day measurement.
Days are counted from baseline_sample_date (first platinum dose), the index date used by every other time variable here. The baseline eGFR is eGFR_CRE_baseline, the same baseline the CKD outcomes are referenced to.
Sign convention: negative means decline. delta_egfr_d90 is eGFR at day 90 - eGFR at baseline, so a fall in kidney function is a negative number. This is the opposite sign to pct_drop in Section 5.16, which is positive for a drop.


Code
DGFR_WINDOW <- 45
DGFR_MARKS  <- c(90, 180, 365)

# Day offsets for the trajectory, measured from baseline_sample_date rather than
# from the pre-baseline creatinine draw that anchors egfr_traj.
dgfr_traj <- egfr_traj %>%
  left_join(final_master %>% select(EMPI, baseline_sample_date), by = "EMPI") %>%
  mutate(cre_day = as.numeric(eGFR_CRE_date - baseline_sample_date)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(cre_day), cre_day > 0)

dgfr_at_mark <- function(traj, mark, window = DGFR_WINDOW) {
  traj %>%
    mutate(.gap = abs(cre_day - mark)) %>%
    filter(.gap <= window) %>%
    group_by(EMPI) %>%
    slice_min(.gap, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    transmute(
      EMPI,
      !!paste0("eGFR_CRE_d", mark)       := round(eGFR_CRE, 1),
      !!paste0("cre_day_d", mark)        := cre_day,
      !!paste0("delta_egfr_d", mark)     := round(eGFR_CRE - eGFR_CRE_baseline, 1),
      !!paste0("delta_egfr_pct_d", mark) := round(
        100 * (eGFR_CRE - eGFR_CRE_baseline) / eGFR_CRE_baseline, 1)
    )
}

for (mk in DGFR_MARKS) {
  final_master <- final_master %>%
    left_join(dgfr_at_mark(dgfr_traj, mk), by = "EMPI")
}

# Availability indicator per mark: 1 if the patient had a creatinine within
# DGFR_WINDOW days of it, 0 otherwise. Carried as its own variable so Table 1
# reports the denominator as n (%) next to the delta it belongs to, rather than
# leaving it in a gtsummary "Unknown" row.
for (mk in DGFR_MARKS) {
  final_master[[paste0("dgfr_avail_d", mk)]] <-
    as.integer(!is.na(final_master[[paste0("delta_egfr_d", mk)]]))
}

# Count of post-baseline creatinine measurements per patient. Needed by the
# coverage table on the analysis pages, which has to separate "no creatinine at
# all" from "creatinine drawn, but never near one of these marks".
final_master <- final_master %>%
  left_join(dgfr_traj %>% count(EMPI, name = "n_cre_post"), by = "EMPI") %>%
  mutate(n_cre_post = ifelse(is.na(n_cre_post), 0L, n_cre_post))

cat("Creatinine available within +/-", DGFR_WINDOW, "days of each mark:\n")


Creatinine available within +/- 45 days of each mark:

  n_ok <- sum(final_master[[paste0("dgfr_avail_d", mk)]] == 1)
  cat(sprintf("  day %3d: %3d / %3d (%.1f%%)\n", mk, n_ok, nrow(final_master),
              100 * n_ok / nrow(final_master)))
}

  d  <- final_master[[paste0("delta_egfr_d", mk)]]
  dp <- final_master[[paste0("delta_egfr_pct_d", mk)]]
  dy <- final_master[[paste0("cre_day_d", mk)]]

  tibble::tibble(
    Mark = paste0("Day ", mk),
    `n with a value` = sum(ok),
    `% with a value in window` = round(100 * sum(ok) / nrow(final_master), 1),
    `Actual day, median [IQR]` = sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]",
      median(dy[ok]), quantile(dy[ok], .25), quantile(dy[ok], .75)),
    `Delta eGFR, median [IQR]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
      median(d[ok]), quantile(d[ok], .25), quantile(d[ok], .75)),
    `Delta eGFR %, median [IQR]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
      median(dp[ok]), quantile(dp[ok], .25), quantile(dp[ok], .75))
  )
})

section: Delta eGFR vs Baseline at 90 / 180 / 365 Days
text:
Delta eGFR vs Baseline at 90 / 180 / 365 Days
Change in creatinine eGFR from eGFR_CRE_baseline, using the creatinine closest to each mark and only when it falls within ± 45 days of it. Days run from baseline_sample_date. Built in Section 5.16b of Data Management and reported per cohort in §2.3 (whole, entire) and §3.3 (carboplatin pages). Descriptive only — not modelled.
Negative means decline, i.e. eGFR at the mark minus eGFR at baseline. This is the opposite sign to pct_drop in the pipeline.

Local/Early (322): day 90 n = 301, Δ 0.9 [−5.9, 7.2]; day 180 n = 244, Δ −2.2 [−12.7, 3.4]; day 365 n = 186, Δ −7.1 [−15.3, −0.5].
The two carboplatin cohorts decline less: carboplatin (189) Δ +2.1 at day 90 and −4.2 at day 365; AUC ≥ 3 (142) Δ +2.1 and −6.0.
Two things to read with it. The realized day is tight — median 86, 179 and 364 against nominal 90, 180 and 365 — so the window is doing its job rather than quietly shifting the timepoint. But coverage falls with time, from 93 % at day 90 to 55 % at day 365, because creatinine is drawn less often once treatment ends. The day-365 figures therefore describe the half of the cohort still being monitored a year out, who are not a random half.
The ± 45-day window matches the pipeline’s existing baseline-lab window (pre_CRE_45days) and is the widest that keeps the 90- and 180-day marks from drawing on the same measurement. Without any window every patient gets a value at every mark, but the closest creatinine to day 365 would be over 276 days away for a tenth of the cohort.

The ± 45-day window matches the window used for every other baseline lab in this pipeline (pre_CRE_45days), and it is the widest window that stops the 90-day and 180-day marks drawing on the same measurement. It costs coverage at the later marks — the n column below shows how much.

dgfr_marks <- c(90, 180, 365)

dgfr_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(dgfr_marks, function(mk) {
  d  <- dat[[paste0("delta_egfr_d", mk)]]

  g  <- dat[[paste0("eGFR_CRE_d", mk)]]
  ok <- !is.na(d)

text:
3.3 Delta eGFR (creatinine) vs Baseline at 90 / 180 / 365 Days
Change in creatinine eGFR from eGFR_CRE_baseline, using the creatinine closest to each mark and taking it only when it falls within ± 45 days of that mark. Days run from baseline_sample_date. Built in Section 5.16b of Data Management.

Negative means decline. delta_egfr_d90 is eGFR at day 90 minus eGFR at baseline, so a fall in kidney function is a negative number — the opposite sign to pct_drop in the data-management pipeline.
The ± 45-day window matches the window used for every other baseline lab in this pipeline (pre_CRE_45days), and it is the widest window that stops the 90-day and 180-day marks drawing on the same measurement. It costs coverage at the later marks — the n column below shows how much.

text:
7.2 Linear model — 365-day delta eGFR on the binary exposure
Adjusted for the same multivariable covariate set as the Fine-Gray models, including the same kidney adjuster — ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys, CKD-EPI Cr-Cys indexed to body surface area (mL/min/1.73m²). Coefficients are mL/min/1.73m² of 365-day eGFR change: a negative coefficient on < -10% means that group declined further.
📄 Download Word table


Code
# .adj_set has three arguments on the whole/entire pages and two on the
# carboplatin pages; call it with whichever this page defines.
.adj_for <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj) {
  if (length(formals(.adj_set)) == 3) .adj_set(pred_var, NULL, egfr_adj)
  else .adj_set(NULL, egfr_adj)
}

lm_d365 <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj = "ckd_epi_idx", docx_name = NULL) {
  adj  <- .adj_for(pred_var, egfr_adj)
  vars <- c(pred_var, adj)
  fmla <- as.formula(paste("delta_egfr_d365 ~", paste(vars, collapse = " + ")))
  tbl_mv <- lm(fmla, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()
  tbl_uv <- tbl_uvregression(
    data = dat %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c("delta_egfr_d365", vars))),
    method = lm, y = delta_egfr_d365,
    pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3))
  out <- tbl_merge(tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
                   tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**"))
  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}

7.2 Linear model — 365-day delta eGFR on the binary exposure
Adjusted for the same multivariable covariate set as the Fine-Gray models, including the same kidney adjuster — ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys, CKD-EPI Cr-Cys indexed to body surface area (mL/min/1.73m²). Coefficients are mL/min/1.73m² of 365-day eGFR change: a negative coefficient on < -10% means that group declined further.
📄 Download Word table


Code
# .adj_set has three arguments on the whole/entire pages and two on the
# carboplatin pages; call it with whichever this page defines.
.adj_for <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj) {
  if (length(formals(.adj_set)) == 3) .adj_set(pred_var, NULL, egfr_adj)
  else .adj_set(NULL, egfr_adj)
}

lm_d365 <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj = "ckd_epi_idx", docx_name = NULL) {
  adj  <- .adj_for(pred_var, egfr_adj)
  vars <- c(pred_var, adj)
  fmla <- as.formula(paste("delta_egfr_d365 ~", paste(vars, collapse = " + ")))
  tbl_mv <- lm(fmla, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()
  tbl_uv <- tbl_uvregression(
    data = dat %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c("delta_egfr_d365", vars))),
    method = lm, y = delta_egfr_d365,
    pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3))
  out <- tbl_merge(tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
                   tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**"))
  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
lm_d365 <- .wrap_tbl(lm_d365)

lm_d365("egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat", docx_name = "sec7_lm_d365")

8.2 Linear model — 365-day delta eGFR on the binary exposure
Adjusted for the same multivariable covariate set as the Fine-Gray models, including the same kidney adjuster — ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys, CKD-EPI Cr-Cys indexed to body surface area (mL/min/1.73m²). Coefficients are mL/min/1.73m² of 365-day eGFR change: a negative coefficient on < -10% means that group declined further.
📄 Download Word table


Code
# .adj_set has three arguments on the whole/entire pages and two on the
# carboplatin pages; call it with whichever this page defines.
.adj_for <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj) {
  if (length(formals(.adj_set)) == 3) .adj_set(pred_var, NULL, egfr_adj)
  else .adj_set(NULL, egfr_adj)
}

lm_d365 <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj = "ckd_epi_idx", docx_name = NULL) {
  adj  <- .adj_for(pred_var, egfr_adj)
  vars <- c(pred_var, adj)
  fmla <- as.formula(paste("delta_egfr_d365 ~", paste(vars, collapse = " + ")))
  tbl_mv <- lm(fmla, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()
  tbl_uv <- tbl_uvregression(
    data = dat %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c("delta_egfr_d365", vars))),
    method = lm, y = delta_egfr_d365,
    pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3))
  out <- tbl_merge(tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
                   tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**"))
  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
lm_d365 <- .wrap_tbl(lm_d365)
